policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere ראתה vs ketiv וראתה differ only by an initial waw. ASV 'Now when Athaliah ... saw that her son was dead, she arose' subordinates the clause with 'when'; English renders both a bare and a waw-prefixed verb this way, and no note is mapped. The English does not distinguish the readings; base fallback retained.

Qere hophal participle המומתים and ketiv polal participle הממותתים both mean 'those being put to death'. ASV 'that were slain' fits either stem; the two notes ('Or, who were'; 'Or, chamber for the beds') are alternative_rendering and do not decide. Base fallback retained.

Qere המאות and ketiv המאיות are orthographic spellings of the same plural 'hundreds'. ASV 'captains over hundreds' cannot reflect the spelling; the notes ('Or, executioners'; 'Hebrew runners') concern other words. Base fallback retained.
Qere המאות and ketiv המאיות are orthographic spellings of the same plural 'hundreds'. ASV 'the captains over hundreds' cannot reflect the spelling; no note is mapped. Base fallback retained.

Qere המאות and ketiv המיאות are orthographic spellings of the same plural 'hundreds'. ASV 'the captains of hundreds' cannot reflect the spelling; no note is mapped. Base fallback retained.

Qere מזבחתיו and ketiv מזבחתו are the standard plene/defective pair for the 3ms suffix on a plural noun, both conventionally read 'his altars'. ASV 'his altars' matches that shared reading and does not exclude the ketiv; the note ('Hebrew offices') concerns another word. Base fallback retained.

Qere המלך (with article) vs ketiv מלך (without) in the construct 'house of the king'. ASV 'the king's house' is definite, but English renders a Hebrew construct chain with 'the' whether or not the nomen rectum carries the article, so the wording does not distinguish the readings; no note is mapped. Base fallback retained.
